introduction: Three people offer different ways to help in the Labyrinth of No Return: a lost adventurer needs a map, a knight seeks nine exact proofs, and Vadatorn asks for three minotaur parts. Each accepted return has its own card. Discovery is separate; new progress requires active, ready accounting.
orientation: ASK ADVENTURER about map or exit. A seasoned explorer declares the exact dusty map among his equipment. The adventurer accepts it for a robe, coins and experience, then departs. This records his accepted return; it does not record your escape from the labyrinth.

ASK KNIGHT about evil or proof. Sir Uthor Whiteheart requests a bat wing, sasquatch hair, beetle shell, poison sac, four different colors of moss and a piece of spider web. Bring all nine exact kinds loose together for his sigil and experience. Repeated copies of one proof cannot replace the others.

The proof sources lie among bats, a sasquatch, beetles, spiders and the moss creatures. The web piece is nested in a large web container. These are declared sources and danger context. Matching goods supplied by another player fit the native return without proof of personal kills or first recovery.

ASK VADATORN about curse or minotaur. His requested tail, heart and eye come from three different minotaurs. Return the exact trio loose together for a quiver and tiny crystal ball. His farewell narrates release from the curse; the journal records acceptance without a separately persisted cure or rescue.

The adventurer suggests speaking to the knight and the Devil after accepting the map. That is a story lead; the three native requests are accepted independently. Hearing a response, carrying a reward or following a conversation order does not complete another return.

The labyrinth includes remote levers, a stone and strange moss that control different passages, alongside locked and hidden doors. Their world descriptions provide clues. Shared access can change the route you need; key possession does not record an unlock, control activation or arrival. The dusty map describes a route whose reliability still needs builder review.

Smedgewack in the tower requests three other goods from here: calcite, a large flask and a small diamond tattoo. His accepted exchange belongs to that foreign recipient. The explorer’s flask is inside his sack; a similarly named item or a map reward cannot replace the exact goods. This lead adds no local achievement.

The rune-like epic node, memory and other treasure have separate purposes. A committed epic claim has its own eligible beneficiaries and authority; humming, touching, gear use or collecting treasure creates no extra local return. Material rows show present loose inventory, while accepted history remains after supplies are spent. Three local returns preserve three achievements and three potential dailies; a daily clock does not guarantee admitted stock.

contacts.description: Declares the exact heart requested by Vadatorn. Encountering or defeating it does not record his accepted trio.

contacts.name: a colorless salamander
contacts.description: Declares a diamondine key for separate doors. Its equipment and ordinary treasure do not substitute for quest proofs.

contacts.name: a spelunking explorer
contacts.description: Declares the dusty map in his equipment and a large flask inside his sack. Recovery, reading and the two recipients’ accepted returns are distinct.

contacts.name: a lost adventurer
contacts.description: Accepts the exact dusty map, rewards the player and then departs. His story leads do not impose a gate on the other two requests.

contacts.name: a knight of the Golden Flame
contacts.description: Accepts nine different exact proofs for the sigil of his order. His public proof list is a clue, not nine keyword achievements.

contacts.name: a battle scarred minotaur
contacts.description: Declares the exact eye requested by Vadatorn. Other minotaur equipment cannot replace the requested parts.

contacts.name: a muscular minotaur
contacts.description: Declares the exact severed tail requested by Vadatorn. A personal kill is separate from accepted custody.

contacts.name: Vadatorn, The Devil Wizard of Despair
contacts.description: Accepts one exact minotaur tail, heart and eye together for two rewards, then departs. A narrated release does not separately persist a cured subject.
